problem:
The total number of pages of a document printed $t$ minutes after printing begins increases at a rate of $\frac{18}{(t+1)^{2}}.$ If, at $t=0$ minutes, the printer had already produced $40$ pages, how many pages will the printer have produced after $2$ minutes?

After $2$ minutes the printer has produced
{{field-1}} pages.

feedback.problem:
The total mass, in kilograms, of compost produced $t$ days after a process begins increases at a rate of $7{e}^{t}.$ If, at $t=0$ days, the process had already produced $5$ kilograms of compost, how much compost will the process have produced after $2$ days?

After $2$ days, the process has produced
{{field-1}} kilograms of compost.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $a(t)=7{e}^{t}$ be the rate at which the amount of compost produced is changing and let $A(T)$ be the amount of compost produced $T$ days after the process begins. 

Using our formula for the accumulation of change, we have

$$
A(T)=A(0)+{\int }_{0}^{T}a(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Substituting the known information and carrying out the necessary integration gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A(T) & =A(0)+{\int }_{0}^{T}a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =5+{\int }_{0}^{T}7{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5+(7{e}^{t}){|}_{0}^{T} \\  & =5+(7{e}^{T})-(7{e}^{0}) \\  & =5+7{e}^{T}-7 \\  & =7{e}^{T}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the amount of compost produced $T=2$ days after the process begins, we substitute in the above:

$$
A(2)=5+7{e}^{2}-7=7{e}^{2}-2.
$$

Thus, after $2$ days, the process has produced $7{e}^{2}-2$ kilograms of compost.
